changes.statement_before:
\begin{definition}[Causal integration]\label{def:iint}
An admissible system satisfies causal integration, written $\Iint(S)=1$, if there is no non-trivial factorization
\[
\Aset=A_1\times A_2,\qquad R=R_1\sqcup R_2,
\]
together with decomposed dynamics and causal structure reproducing admissible histories within error smaller than a positive margin $\delta_{\mathrm{int}}(S)$ while preserving $\Id_S$.
More explicitly, this shorthand is relative to a declared admissible
factorization class.  For such a class $\mathfrak{D}$, write
$\Iint(S;\mathfrak{D})=1$ when no factorization in $\mathfrak{D}$
reproduces the admissible histories below a positive margin
$\delta_{\mathrm{int}}(S;\mathfrak{D})$ while preserving $\Id_S$.
The unqualified notation $\Iint(S)=1$ refers to the default structural class
$\mathfrak{D}_{\ast}$: fixed, time-homogeneous, schedule-independent,
non-trivial product factorizations with both factors non-singleton, with
split readouts $R=R_1\sqcup R_2$, decomposed dynamics and causal structure, a
search space normalized independently of the target error, and no
reconstruction decoder or time-dependent post-processing map that re-couples
the factors at output time.  This default structural reading is the adopted
class recorded in
\texttt{\detokenize{docs/}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{ai-}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{platform-}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{outputs/}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{analysis/}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{QICN_}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{IINT_}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{CANONICA}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{L_}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{CLASS_}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{SPLIT_}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{READOUT.}\allowbreak{}\detokenize{md}}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Non-null differentiation]\label{def:idiff}
An admissible system satisfies non-null differentiation, written $\Idiff(S)=1$, if there exist $x,y\in\Aset$, a horizon $T$, and a readout subfamily $\Read^\star\subseteq R$ such that
\[
\dist\bigl(h_{S,T}(x;u_\bullet),h_{S,T}(y;u_\bullet)\bigr)\ge \delta_{\mathrm{diff}}(S)>0
\]
for some admissible schedule $u_\bullet$, and if the null class $\nullclass$ is not an asymptotically stable admissible attractor.
\end{definition}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{remark}[Class-relative integration margin]
The integration criterion is class-relative.  Adopting
$\mathfrak{D}_{\ast}$ does not assert that $S$ resists every broader
behavioral simulator.  In particular, under decoder-coupled or
schedule-dependent behavioral classes such as
$\mathfrak{D}_{\mathrm{approx}}$, the corresponding margin
$\delta_{\mathrm{int}}(S;\mathfrak{D}_{\mathrm{approx}})$ may vanish, i.e. may
be equal to $0$; the
current coupled-carrier analysis records precisely this failure mode.  Thus
the default structural reading preserves a falsation surface and must not be
read as an unconditional closure of integration, nor as a strengthening of any
downstream theorem that assumes $\Iint(S)=1$.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Admissible comparative evidence]
A dataset pair $(D_h,D_m)$ is admissible under $\mathfrak{E}$ only if the
following predicates are all true:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $D_h,D_m$ are measurable finite samples from
  $(\mathcal{T},\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{T}))$.
  \item The preregistered protocol hash, control manifest hash, and analysis
  shell hash match their frozen records.
  \item Human-side records are not generated, rewritten, or completed by
  synthetic systems: $\epsilon_{\mathrm{syn}}=0$ for the human channel.
  \item Blinding leakage is bounded by the preregistered budget:
  $\mathbb{P}(\mathrm{leak})\leq \epsilon_{\mathrm{blind}}$.
  \item Every declared negative control has an executed and timestamped outcome
  under the same admissibility grammar.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Cryptographic freeze map]
Let $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{config}}$ be the set of canonical preregistration
configurations after deterministic serialization. A freeze map is a

\begin{equation}
H:\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{config}}\to\{0,1\}^{256}.

\begin{definition}[Blind adjudicator loss]
For $a(Y)\in\{h,m,\mathtt{tie}\}$ and a declared $\gamma\in[1/2,1]$, put
\[
 L_\gamma(a(Y),\ell)=
 {\bf1}\{a(Y)\ne\ell,\ a(Y)\ne\mathtt{tie}\}
 +\gamma{\bf1}\{a(Y)=\mathtt{tie}\}.
\]
Report $R_\gamma=\mathbb E L_\gamma$, coverage $C=\Pr(a(Y)\ne\mathtt{tie})$, and error conditional on coverage when $C>0$. For acceptance require a preregistered $C\ge C_{\min}>0$. Forced choice has $C=1$; always abstaining has $C=0$ and $R_\gamma=\gamma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Null error lower bound]\label{thm:null-forced}
Let $E$ denote leakage and $p=\Pr(E)$. If in the clean stratum $\ell$ is balanced conditional on $Y,E^c$, then
\[
 R_\gamma(a)\ge(1-p)/2.
\]
Alternatively, suppose $Y$ is coupled to a clean bundle $Y_0$ for which $\ell$ is balanced conditional on $Y_0$, and $Y=Y_0$ outside an event of probability at most $p$. Then
\[
 R_\gamma(a)\ge\max\{0,1/2-p\}.
\]
The assumptions are distinct. Under the first, revealing the label on a leak event independent of the balanced label can attain the bound with forced choice.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp Leakage Bounds at Fixed Coverage]\label{thm:coverage-sensitive-leakage}
Writing $z_+=\max\{0,z\}$, the clean-stratum and coupling nulls of Theorem~\ref{thm:null-forced} respectively give
\[
 B_{\rm clean}(C,p)=\gamma(1-C)+\tfrac12(C-p)_+,\qquad
 B_{\rm coup}(C,p)=\gamma(1-C)+(C/2-p)_+ .
\]
Both are sharp for each $C,p\in[0,1]$, with balanced marginal labels and leak probability at most $p$, including selective abstention. Minimizing over coverage gives the bounds of Theorem~\ref{thm:null-forced}.
\end{theorem}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{theorem}[Independent-Block Risk and Coverage Inference]\label{thm:independent-block-risk-intervals}
Let $M$ count covered decisions and $K$ count wrong covered decisions among $n$ independent blocks. Then
\[
 M\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,C),\qquad K\mid M\sim\operatorname{Bin}(M,e),
 \qquad e=\Pr(W=1\mid B=1)\quad(C>0).
\]
With $I_C=I_{\alpha_C}(M,n)$ and $I_e=I_{\alpha_e}(K,M)$, simultaneous coverage is at least $1-\alpha_C-\alpha_e$. When $M=0$ retain $I_e=[0,1]$ and leave sample conditional error unreported. The minimum and maximum of $\gamma(1-c)+cx$ over the corners of $I_C\times I_e$ give risk bounds simultaneous with $I_C$.

A direct joint alternative uses counts $N=(K,M-K,n-M)$ and probabilities $\theta=(Ce,C(1-e),1-C)$. Let $f_\theta$ be their multinomial mass and define
\[
 p_\theta(N)=\sum_{\substack{m_1+m_2+m_3=n\\f_\theta(m)\le f_\theta(N)}} f_\theta(m),
 \qquad \mathcal Q_\alpha(N)=\{\theta:p_\theta(N)>\alpha\}.
\]
Projecting $\mathcal Q_\alpha$ onto $C=\theta_1+\theta_2$ and $R_\gamma=\theta_1+\gamma\theta_3$, using infima and suprema, yields a simultaneous exact confidence region with coverage at least $1-\alpha$.

Suppose a justified leak cap is $p_U$. For a stochastic audit, let an audit flag $D$ satisfy $\mathbf1_E\le D$ almost surely in the same target population. From $J$ flags in $n_D$ independent audit blocks, the upper endpoint of $I_{\alpha_D}(J,n_D)$ can supply $p_U$. With simultaneous coverage endpoints $C_L,C_U$ and risk upper endpoint $R_U$, certify the preregistered minimum coverage and a fixed positive margin $\eta$ against the applicable null floor only if
\[
 C_L\ge C_{\min},\qquad R_U\le B_\star(C_U,p_U)-\eta .
\]
Under that null this certification has probability at most $\alpha_C+\alpha_e+\alpha_D$ for the rectangle construction, or $\alpha+\alpha_D$ for the joint construction. A deterministic certified cap uses $\alpha_D=0$.
\end{theorem}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{theorem}[Stationary AR(1) Likelihood and GLS]\label{thm:stationary-ar1-likelihood-gls}
For a block of length $n\ge1$ let $e_t=y_t-\mu_t$. Assume Gaussian $e_1\sim N(0,\sigma^2/(1-\rho^2))$ and innovations $e_t-\rho e_{t-1}\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ independent of each other and of $e_1$, with $|\rho|<1$ and $\sigma^2>0$. Then
\[
 Q_\rho(e)=(1-\rho^2)e_1^2+\sum_{t=2}^n(e_t-\rho e_{t-1})^2,
\]
\[
 \log f(y\mid\mu,\rho,\sigma^2)
 =-\frac n2\log(2\pi\sigma^2)+\frac12\log(1-\rho^2)
 -\frac{Q_\rho(y-\mu)}{2\sigma^2}.
\]
For two frozen mean models sharing the covariance, the log-density ratio in favor of $A$ is $(Q_\rho(e_B)-Q_\rho(e_A))/(2\sigma^2)$. With full-column-rank design $X$ and fixed common covariance, GLS uniquely minimizes $Q_\rho(y-X\beta)$ at
\[
 \widehat\beta=(X^\top A_\rho X)^{-1}X^\top A_\rho y,\qquad
 Q_\rho(e)=e^\top A_\rho e .
\]
\end{theorem}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{proposition}[Operational closure of a comparative program]
The comparative program reaches operational closure only when there exists a
predeclared alignment map $T:\mathcal{T}\to\mathcal{Z}$ into a common Polish
feature space $(\mathcal{Z},d_{\mathcal{Z}})$ and the total divergence
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\mathrm{comp}} =
  \lambda_1 W_1(T_{\#}\widehat{\mu}_h,T_{\#}\widehat{\mu}_m)
  + \lambda_2 D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat{p}_h\Vert \widehat{p}_m)
  + \lambda_3 \max_k |\sigma_k(D_h)-\sigma_k(D_m)|
\end{equation}
is defined and satisfies the frozen budget
$\Delta_{\mathrm{comp}}\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{budget}}$. This closure is a
precondition for comparative interpretation, not a claim of consciousness,
identity, or substrate equivalence.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Joint Local Certificate and Causal Selectivity]\label{prop:bridge-six-port-certificate}
The six tasks have simultaneous normalized margin lower bounds
\[
 (m_D,m_V,m_W,m_A,m_E,m_T)\ \ge\
 \left(\tfrac14,\tfrac7{16},\tfrac{13}{96},\tfrac14,
       \tfrac{31}{32},\tfrac12-\tfrac{64}{19683}\right).
\]
Their minimum is $13/96>1/16$. Six concrete lesions have the following local certificate-presence matrix, with columns in order D,V,W,A,E,T:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}
 \text{intact}&1&1&1&1&1&1\\
 I_D&0&1&0&1&1&1\\
 I_V&1&0&1&1&1&1\\
 I_W&1&0&0&1&1&1\\
 I_A&1&1&1&0&1&1\\
 I_E&1&0&1&1&0&1\\
 I_T&1&1&1&1&1&0
\end{array}
\]
The matrix of losses from the intact row has rank six. For aggregate rivals retaining at least one declared structural deficiency, maximum normalized task loss has a joint margin at least $5/192$. A nonnegative complexity penalty preserves that last margin whenever its additional candidate cost is smaller than $5/192$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Coercivity for Latent Distance Recovery]\label{prop:projection-coercivity-bounds}
If $X$ is metric and on pairs in each restricted fibre
\[
 c\,d_X(x,x')\le d_Z(F(x),F(x'))\le L\,d_X(x,x')
 \qquad (c>0,\ L\ge0),
\]
then $c\,\operatorname{diam}_X(A\cap\pi^{-1}(y))\le D_y
\le L\,\operatorname{diam}_X(A\cap\pi^{-1}(y))$.
Uniform error $\varepsilon$ entails a latent fibre diameter at most $2\varepsilon/c$. For scalar $F$ the upper bound alone gives a sufficient error budget of $(L/2)$ times the supremum of the latent diameters. In a sector where distance is recovered directly from observations, a bound $c_\pi d_X(x,x')\le d_Y(\pi x,\pi x')$ with $c_\pi>0$ gives the inverse-distance bound there.
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[Projected two-port system]\label{def:bridge-two-port-system}
Let $x=(p,\theta,b,m)$ belong to the writable support of Papers V--VIII, with native transition $F_c$ and readout $R$. Adjoin body and world vectors $\mathbf b,\mathbf w\in[-1,1]^2$. Put
\[
 \alpha=\beta=h=\tfrac14,\quad \chi=\tfrac18,\quad
 J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 L_0=\tfrac12(I+J),\quad
 Q_+=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The indexed frame $P(p)$ is the swap matrix at role profile $p_1$ and the identity at every other catalogue profile. For a world projection $Q\in\{I,Q_+\}$, an evaluation map $L$ with $\|L\|_\infty\le1$, a motor gain $|\mu|\le1$, and an evaluation switch $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, define
\begin{align*}
 x'&=F_c(x), &s&=P(p)Q\mathbf w, &f&=\chi L(s-\mathbf b),\\
 \mathbf b'&=\alpha\mathbf b+\beta s+\varepsilon f+a_{\rm b},\\
 \mathbf w'&=\alpha Q\mathbf w+\beta\mu QP(p)^{-1}\mathbf b+Qd.
\end{align*}
Here $a_{\rm b},d\in[-h,h]^2$ are distinct body and world input ports. Normal evaluation uses $L=L_0$. Native lifts use $Q=I$, $\mu=1$, $\varepsilon=0$ and zero port inputs. The native and additional readouts are respectively $R\pi$ and $(\mathbf b,\mathbf w)$, where $\pi(x,\mathbf b,\mathbf w)=x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact Projection, Stability and Inherited Certificates]\label{thm:bridge-port-preservation}
Every lifted update satisfies $\pi\widetilde F_{c,a_{\rm b},d}=F_c\pi$. The section $\iota(x)=(x,0,0)$ is invariant under native lifts. On a common profile, use
\[
 \widetilde d=\max\{d_{\rm core},\|\Delta\mathbf b\|_\infty/4,
                                      \|\Delta\mathbf w\|_\infty/4\}.
\]
The native branch contraction remains at most $9/16$. The entire intervened port family contracts in its fibre by at most $3/4$ under common inputs and preserves $[-1,1]^4$. All previously certified native protocols, with their original readouts, comparison sectors and information budgets, have exactly the same records and margins in this extension.
\end{theorem}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{theorem}[Motor Closure with Preserved Early Competence]\label{thm:bridge-motor-closure}
At $g=1$ the second and third body responses are independent of the motor sign. In each common-mode component the fourth response is
\[
 y_4(\tau)=h(3\alpha^2\beta+\tau\beta^3),\qquad s_E=h\beta^3=1/256.
\]
Its gap is $2s_E$, and the residual $y_4-(3\alpha/2)y_3$ is $\tau s_E$. Every rival without the motor edge, under the stated modularity, has uniform fourth-response error at least $s_E$. Cutting the edge removes the residual without changing the second or third responses. Common-mode world compression preserves this motor test exactly.
\end{theorem}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{criterion}[Bridge realization non-emptiness burden]\label{thm:bridge-realization-exists}
Any claim that the full bridge predicate package is non-empty must exhibit a
typed realization satisfying the predicate definitions, rival comparisons,
intervention contracts, artifact gates, and interpretation boundaries together.
Setting all formal predicate flags to true is only a syntactic witness and does
not count as realization evidence.
\end{criterion}

changes.statement_before:
\begin{conjecture}[Predicate independence burden]\label{thm:predicate-independence}
The bridge predicate family should be independent only if, for each predicate
slot, there exists an admissible witness model that toggles that slot while
holding the remaining bridge burden package fixed under the same comparator,
intervention, artifact, and governance constraints. The current text supplies
the burden grammar, not a completed independence proof.
\end{conjecture}
